files.purpose: Hydra.swift is the model and prompt layer of Hydra, the mode in which one chat's agent (the lead) sends helper agents called heads out in parallel: it defines the persisted pair/profile configuration (HydraPair, HydraHeadProfile), the launch-time resolution (HydraLaunch), the per-head record kept on head threads (HydraHeadInfo, HydraLanding), the 25-name persona roster with colours and dragon-head assets, and the Droppy-run head time/tool budget constants. Its largest part, the HydraPrompts enum, holds every English text the app puts in front of a lead or a head (native policy for Claude/Codex/Copilot, fallback policy for all other providers, worker/scout system prompts, report/merge/turn notes, refusal and dropped-block notices), the native agent definitions for Claude --agents, Copilot customAgents and Codex config overrides, and the parser for the fenced ```hydra delegation block (find, strip, mark sent/leaving, parse whole-block). In 1.6.2 it also gained HydraDelegationBudget, a value type holding the per-request round and refusal counters plus a one-shot dropped-block notice that ThreadRuntime keeps as `hydraBudget`.

Suffix detail (:276): `if let space = bare.lastIndex(of: " "), Int(bare[bare.index(after: space)...]) != nil` searches only U+0020 and accepts anything Swift Int(String) parses, including signed forms, so "Otto -1" and "Otto +2" are stripped to "Otto" and match index 3, while "Otto\t2" (tab) is not stripped and matches nothing (nil). persona(named:) then uses the round only when it is > 1 ("Otto -1" gives plain Otto).

HydraDelegationBudget: canDelegate = rounds < HydraPrompts.maxDelegationRounds (3). beginTurn(userAuthored:) resets rounds and refusals only when userAuthored (documented as `hydraHeads == nil` at turn start); it never clears dropNotice. chargeRound increments rounds. refuse(message): if refusals < maxRefusals (3) increments refusals and returns true (refusal gets its own turn); otherwise calls noteDropped(message) and returns false. noteDropped sets dropNotice = HydraPrompts.droppedBlockNotice(message) (overwrites any previous one). takeDropNotice returns dropNotice and clears it (defer).

readOpener state machine (bytes, ASCII-lowercased for A-Z): states 0-2 count backticks (96), any other byte resets to 0; state 3: space(32), tab(9) and further backticks are skipped, 'h'(104) -> 4, else 0; states 4-7 expect 'y'(121) 'd'(100) 'r'(114) 'a'(97), mismatch -> 1 if the byte is a backtick else 0; state 8 (after 'hydra'): '-'(45) -> 9, else readOpenerEnd; states 9-12 expect 's' 'e' 'n' 't', same mismatch rule; states 13 and 14 -> readOpenerEnd; state 15 (after CR) needs LF(10) to enter the body, else reset. readOpenerEnd: space/tab -> 14, CR(13) -> 15, LF(10) -> body, else reset (1 on backtick). So the parser accepts ```hydra and ```hydra-sent (with any case, optional spaces/tabs, CRLF), and also four or more leading backticks; it does not accept hydra-leaving.

files.purpose: MCP.swift defines the data model of Droppy Code's MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector support: how a catalog server is reached (stdio, streamable HTTP, or OAuth behind the app's local proxy), the fields a user must type, the category list, the catalog entry, the resolved launchable server, probe results, the per-server persisted connection state, setup guides and the connection state enum. It also implements placeholder filling ({key} substitution with host normalisation) and resolution of an entry into an MCPResolvedServer, and fixes the on-disk locations of mcp.json, custom-mcp.json and the per-provider config files claude.json, codex.json and copilot.json.

fill(text, values): for each field in declaration order, value = values[key] if non-empty, else field.defaultValue, else "". If the text contains "://{key}" (placeholder standing as a URL host), the value is trimmed, a leading "https://" and then "http://" prefix are removed case-insensitively (the loop checks both in that order on the progressively stripped value), and all trailing "/" are removed; then every occurrence of "{key}" in the text is replaced (so the normalised value is also used for any other occurrence of the same token). Doc example: `https://gitlab.example.com/` becomes `gitlab.example.com`. Only declared `fields` are iterated (:137), so a `{token}` in args, env values, headers or url whose key is not a field is left literally in the output. `values[field.key].flatMap { $0.isEmpty ? nil : $0 }` (:138) treats only the exact empty string as untyped: a whitespace-only value is used as typed (not replaced by defaultValue), and trimming (.trimmed) happens only in the "://{key}" host case (:140-141).
oauthURL(values:) returns fill(url) for .oauth, nil otherwise.

resolve(values:): .stdio -> command copied unfilled, args filled, env values filled and entries whose filled value is empty dropped (an optional field left empty drops its variable rather than passing ""); .http -> url filled, headers filled and empty-valued headers dropped; .oauth -> url = MCPProxy.url(for: id) and oauthUpstream = fill(url). The proxy route is MCPProxy.url(for:) (MCPProxy.swift:35-37) = "http://127.0.0.1:\(port)/mcp/\(serverID)", so an OAuth server resolves to url "http://127.0.0.1:<proxy port>/mcp/<catalog id>".

files.purpose: MCPCustom.swift models MCP servers the user defines in Settings › MCP › Custom: a stdio command with arguments and environment variable names, or a streamable-HTTP URL with header names, stored lean in custom-mcp.json without any variable values. It turns a custom definition into an MCPCatalogEntry so connecting, probing, the Keychain, provider configs and the key panel treat it like a built-in server, and it holds the editor's save validation (MCPCustomError) with its user-facing messages, the variable-key rule and the remote-URL rule (https anywhere, http only for localhost).
